correctness.rationale: Each nonempty face corresponds to the product of its commuting primary factors; this is equivariant under conjugation. The prime labels are pairwise distinct and invariant under conjugation, so a setwise stabilizer fixes a simplex pointwise. More strongly, equality of two quotient points from one closed simplex forces equality of the barycentric coordinate at each prime and hence equality of points. Orbit-simplex closures thus give cells, with alternating boundary signs in increasing prime order and no stabilizer multiplicities. Deleting the p-factor acts on a length-L cycle by a power whose exponent has gcd p^v_p(L) with L; this gives the stated split into p^v_p(L) equal cycles. Four distinct primes require at least 17 letters: assign each prime to a cycle it divides, whose length is at least the product of its assigned primes, at least their sum. The same bound with three primes excludes triangles before 10. Independent exact enumeration and boundary reconstruction checked ∂₁∂₂=0 and gave C₂ counts (1,2,5,9,15,24) at n=10,…,15, with peeling rounds [1], [2], [5], [8,1], [12,3], [15,4,1]. A uniquely incident triangle on a remaining edge must have coefficient zero in any integral cycle, so peeling preserves the two-cycle group. The last four simplices at n=15 are exactly the specified disjoint-prime cycles; their edge and vertex labels and orbit identifications are precisely those of a tetrahedral boundary. Its six edge equations force all integral triangle coefficients to be a common integer times (1,−1,1,−1); this agrees with the independent residual rank 3 and verifies primitivity and exhaustion. Since there are no three-cells, the cycle generates H₂, and injectivity below 15 gives the sharp first occurrence (also covering empty Y₁).
residual_risks: No computation of H₂ beyond 15 or of other homology degrees is implied. The subspace is an embedded sphere, not a claimed wedge summand of the geometric quotient.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A simplicial complex keeping only prime supports admits a section into this quotient by choosing one cycle of each of those primes and the rest fixed; this readily supplies the tetrahedral boundary at 15. It does not prove that the quotient has no earlier classes or no further classes at 15, since many other cells share those same supports. The full integral boundary calculation is the substantive conclusion.

value.rationale: The group clique complex and its conjugacy-class schematic motivate asking which integral cycles actually survive in the associated geometric orbit space. The exact first occurrence, exhaustion of H₂, and embedded primitive representative identify a specific qualitative transition, which would not follow from prime supports alone. It is a reproducible benchmark for studies of group-complex quotients even without an all-n homology theorem.
residual_risks: The verified result is a sharp finite cutoff only; it cannot substitute for topology of the unquotiented complex, for order-sheaf homology, or for a full homotopy classification.
